title.en: The Ant, the Sluggard, and Seven Things God Hates

body.en:
This chapter gives several short, punchy warnings. First: don't rashly guarantee someone else's debt without thinking it through carefully — it can trap you in obligations you never meant to take on.

Then comes one of the most famous passages in all of Proverbs: 'Go to the ant, you sluggard; consider its ways and be wise! It has no commander, no overseer or ruler, yet it stores its provisions in summer and gathers its food at harvest.'

The lazy person is warned directly: 'How long will you lie there, you sluggard? When will you get up from your sleep?' A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to rest — and poverty comes like a thief, suddenly!

Then the chapter lists things the Lord specifically detests: 'haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood, a heart that devises wicked schemes, feet that are quick to rush into evil, a false witness who pours out lies, and a person who stirs up conflict in the community.'

Seven specific things, named clearly — a vivid, memorable list of exactly the kind of character God hates, and by contrast, the kind of character wisdom builds instead.

verse.en: Go to the ant, you sluggard; consider its ways and be wise!

label.en: Activity sheet: The Ant, the Sluggard, and Seven Things God Hates

body.en:
Big idea: two of the most vivid, memorable passages in all of Proverbs — the diligent ant (a brilliant, concrete picture for children of self-motivated hard work) and the specific, named list of things God hates, giving children a clear, tangible vocabulary for character rather than vague generalities. Both passages model Proverbs' characteristic method: making abstract virtue concrete through unforgettable imagery.

Conversation starters: (1) What can an ant teach a person about hard work, even without anyone telling it what to do? (2) Why might "a little" laziness lead to poverty "like a thief" — suddenly and unexpectedly? (3) Which of the seven things God hates in this list do you think is most tempting to overlook as "not a big deal"?

Pray for diligence like the ant's, and for hearts that genuinely hate what God hates.
